newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CHIPPER HOMERS TWICE AS BRAVES WIN BATTLE OF JONES BOYS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CHIPPER HOMERS TWICE AS BRAVES WIN BATTLE OF JONES BOYS.

text.p: Chipper won the battle of the Jones Boys Wednesday, homering twice including his first career grand slam as the Atlanta Braves pounded Bobby Jones and the Mets 14-7 to avoid a three-game series sweep.
Chipper Jones, who has 12 homers this season and four career multi-homer games, was 3-for-3 and scored four times. He tied a career high with five runs batted in.

"This win was good for us in that it got us back on track in terms of head-to-head with the Mets," he said. "They are full of confidence right now and for us to score the runs that we did against their ace, it speaks volumes of our character."

Bobby Jones (12-4), who captured nine of his last 10 starts and entered the game with the most wins in the majors, had the worst outing of his career. He was tagged for 10 runs -- six earned -- and 11 hits with four walks in 4 2/3 innings.

"I just didn't feel as sharp as I normally do," he said. "I walked four guys. That's really not me and every pitch that I made a mistake on they took full advantage off and hit as hard as a good hitting team would."

Fred McGriff and Ryan Klesko also had three hits each for the Braves, who collected 17 in all -- the most allowed by the Mets this season. Jeff Blauser added a solo homer in the ninth. The 14 runs were the most yielded by New York this season.
The Mets had thrilling rallies for wins Monday and Tuesday to extend their winning streak to six games, but the Braves decided the series finale early, scoring 10 times in the first five innings.
Tom Glavine (8-4) got the win.

In Los Angeles, Ismael Valdes missed out on a chance for his first complete game since 1995 and Mike Piazza continued his torrid hitting with a two-run homer to lead the Dodgers to a 2-0 victory over the Colorado Rockies.

Valdes (4-8) scattered four hits, walking none and striking out eight before tiring with one out in the ninth. He also picked up his first hit of the year, a bunt-single in the third, breaking an 0-for-27 skid.
Darren Hall retired the final batter for his second save in two days in the absence of closer Todd Worrell, who is out with a stomach virus.
Piazza, who has 13 RBI in his last 15 games, provided the scoring by driving a 2-1 offering from starter John Burke (2-2) over the centre-field wall in the first inning.
In San Francisco, Damon Berryhill and Jose Vizcaino had two-run singles in a six-run eighth inning as the Giants pounded out a season-high 17 hits in a 14-7 defeat of the San Diego Padres.
The inning matched the Giants' largest of the season and turned an 8-7 game into a blowout.

San Diego starter Andy Ashby (3-4) allowed eight runs -- seven earned -- and 12 hits in six innings, walking four and striking out four. Doug Bochtler was charged with for all six runs in the eighth, retiring just one batter.
J.T. Snow tied a career-high with four RBI for the Giants.
In St Louis, Gary Gaetti's two-run homer with one out in the ninth inning off reliever Terry Adams lifted the Cardinals to a 3-1 victory over the Chicago Cubs.

Gaetti supplied all the offence for the Cardinals, singling home Dmitri Young in the second inning and then ending the game by driving the first pitch from Adams (1-3) over the right-centre field wall for his sixth homer.
T.J. Mathews (3-3) pitched two hitless innings in relief of starter Matt Morris to notch the Cards' fourth win in their last five games.
In Houston, Darryl Kile and Billy Wagner combined on a six-hitter and James Mouton had a two-run double in a four-run eighth inning as the Astros beat the Pittsburgh Pirates 5-1.

Kile (9-3), who has won eight of his last nine decisions, allowed one run, six hits and two walks with seven strikeouts. The right-hander has gone at least seven innings in 15 of 16 starts this season.
Wagner struck out the side in the ninth for Houston, which has won four of its last six contests.

In Philadelphia, John Cangelosi went 4-for-5 with three RBI and Alex Fernandez (8-6) settled down after a shaky first inning to earn his fourth straight win as the Florida Marlins defeated the Phillies 7-5.
Florida (45-30) moved 15 games over .500 for the first time in the five-year history of the franchise. The Marlins also won a series at Philadelphia for the first time, taking two of three.
The loss was the 10th in 11 games for the Phillies.
In Montreal, Mike Kelly's two-out homer in the top of the 11th lifted the Cincinnati Reds past the Expos 2-1.

Montreal took a 1-0 lead in the first when Mike Lansing smacked a 1-2 pitch over the left-field fence. It was his 12th homer, tying the franchise record by a second baseman established in 1975 by Pete Mackanin.
